title: Police to increase patrols downtown amid safety concerns, neighborhood group says
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Boston to increase downtown police patrols after violent incidents, focusing on areas like Boston Common and Winter Street.
A recent meeting with 77 stakeholders led by DBNA aimed to address rising crime and illicit activities.
Boston faces police staffing shortages, with 2,100 officers instead of the required 2,500, complicating increased patrol efforts.

title: All four ‘Lord of the Rings’ movie Hobbits explored Boston together this weekend
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Sean Astin, Elijah Wood, Dominic Monaghan, and Billy Boyd reunited for Fan Expo Boston and explored the city.
The actors dined at La Royal Cambridge and visited Neptune Oyster and The Green Dragon pub.
They celebrated 25 years of 'Lord of the Rings' with an event titled 'An Evening with the Hobbits.'

title: Jaylen Brown to host free Boston block party at Boston Common on Aug. 30
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: Jaylen Brown will host '741 Frequency Fest' at Boston Common on August 30 from 2-7 p.m.
The free block party is Brown's way to thank Boston fans before joining the Philadelphia 76ers.
The event includes music, games, giveaways, and is located at the Charles Street entrance.

title: Patriots reportedly releasing 2024 third-round pick Caedan Wallace
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Patriots reportedly plan to release Caedan Wallace, their 2024 third-round draft pick and offensive lineman.
Wallace, picked 68th overall in 2024, played 10 games over two seasons with reduced playing time in 2025.
Releasing Wallace would leave Drake Maye and Marcellas Dial Jr. as the only 2024 draft picks on the Patriots roster.

title: Comedian Matt Rife throws down with a paranormal investigator over ‘haunted’ event in Salem
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Comedian Matt Rife told a paranormal investigator to commit suicide in a comment about a haunted event in Salem.
Rife's remarks were directed at Chris Mac after Mac commented on a Salem Witch Trials event announcement on social media.
Followers of Mac, who is autistic, criticized Rife's comments, prompting both individuals to delete their posts.

title: Hunter Henry agrees to a two-year extension with the Patriots
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Hunter Henry signs a two-year contract extension with the New England Patriots worth up to $20 million.
The extension includes $14.5 million guaranteed and a $4.2 million signing bonus, according to media reports.
Henry has been crucial in the Patriots' offense since joining in 2021, with 259 catches and 26 touchdowns.

title: 83-year-old drives Jaguar into Acton CVS, causing major damage
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: An 83-year-old woman crashed a Jaguar into an Acton CVS, causing significant damage to the store.
The driver and her 88-year-old passenger were unharmed; no shoppers or employees were injured in the incident.
The store will remain closed for repairs; Acton Police requested the driver's license be suspended or revoked.

title: Logan runway closure this fall could mean more flight delays
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Logan Airport's Runway 27 will close for 75 days starting August 31 for safety upgrades.
The closure will reduce runway capacity, possibly causing delays, especially in poor weather conditions.
Nearby communities may experience more flights and construction noise due to the runway closure.

title: One dead, 3 injured in head-on crash on the Cape
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A head-on crash in Sandwich, Massachusetts, on Sunday night left one person dead and three injured.
The collision involved a 2011 Toyota Prius and a 2017 Toyota RAV4 on Farmersville Road at 8:50 p.m.
The Prius driver died at Cape Cod Hospital; the three in the RAV4 sustained nonlife-threatening injuries.

title: Driver on South Shore narrowly escaped before commuter train totaled his Camry
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 33-year-old delivery driver made a wrong turn onto railroad tracks and exited before a train struck his car.
The incident occurred Sunday at 12:23 a.m. in Cohasset on the MBTA Commuter Rail Greenbush Line; no injuries reported.
North Main Street closed for over two hours as Cohasset Police investigated; driver and train passengers uninjured.
